committee led by Chairperson, Mr. Watson Castillo. Overall, 20,000 acres of

grazing conditions within these operators designated allotments and ultimately would also serve
to improve watershed function within the Torreon Wash Subbasin of the Rio Puerco Watershed.

Objectives:
The proposed action is to improve watershed function by improving soil and vegetative conditions by
implementing management of Wyoming big sagebrush on public land. This EA is being written to
analyze sagebrush treatments through chemical means. Treatments would be implemented when
sagebrush grassland habitats are found to deviate from ecological site descriptions and or desired plant
community.
Planned_Implementation:
Tebuthiuron would be applied at a rate of 0.3 lbs. per acre active ingredient to achieve an approximately
85% removal (kill) of the dominant sagebrush vegetation, and at 0.5 lbs. on heavier clay soils to achieve
the same rate of kill. Tebuthiuron would be applied at a 100' swath width while leaving 100&$ buffer zones
of nontreatment adjacent to non-suitable ecological sites or soils. Also, for every J 000 acres of treated
area the BLM will leave 100 acres of untreated area within or directly adjacent to the treated area for use
by wild1ife and other sage obligate species. In some areas there is considerable juniper encroachment of
deeper soil sites and sagebrush grassland communities. It is anticipated that a rate of 0.31bs a.i/ac is
likely to kill less than 50% of those trees, while achieving the approximate 85% kill on sagebrush.
Pinyon/juniper is not being targeted unless it has encroached into ecological sites and is contributing to a
deviation from the desired plant community.

Trt_Concerns_Desc:
The areas that will be considered for treatment have basically shifted from grassland to a shrubland and or
sage/grass community vegetation type consisting primarily of Artemisia tridentata spp.Wyoming big
sage. A herbaceous understory consisting primarily of undesirably low levels of galleta, blue grama, sand
dropseed, Indian ricegrass, western wheatgrass, and bottlebrush Squirreltail, occurring on sandy to loamy
upland soils, with high levels of bare soil exists. The encroachment of sagebrush, considered by many as
an invasive woody plant species (Whitson, T.D. (ed) et al.1996), has been replacing the once dominant
natural grasslands. The proposed projects should help restore the sites toward a more desired plant
community, and in this area possibly more sustainable than their potential natural plant community, by
increasing vegetative ground cover and diversity, thus reducing runoff and erosion.

Objectives:
The objective of the vegetation treatments is to reduce sagebrush composition by 40-70% in
those identified areas, which would promote increases in herbaceous vegetation. Some
juniper trees within the treatment area would also be susceptible to mortality by the herbicide.
An adequate native seed source exists to propagate herbaceous vegetation after the vegetation
treatment, precluding the need for reseeding. The treatment areas would be deferred from
livestock grazing for 1 to 2 growing seasons.
Planned_Implementation:
Aerial application of the spike pellets would be via a fixed-wing aircraft similar to those used
for crop dusting. The pilot would be required to have a pesticide applicators license and the
airplane would need to be equipped to precisely dispense the spike pellets. A backpack
blower would be used for the ground application, with the applicator using an A TV and
walking, in combination to assist in creating irregular edges. Spike would be applied at a rate
of .3 to .4 lbs. of active ingredient per acre. The preferred time of application would be from
September to November (specific dates are not yet known), however the material could be
applied anytime as long as the ground is not frozen, water saturated or covered by snow.

The purpose of the action is to improve approximately 1200 acres of
sagebrush/grass vegetation to a condition that meets the fundamentals of
rangeland health as described in43 CFR 4180.1 (a-d) in addition to moving

grasses, 5 to 10% forbs, and 25 to 30% sagebrush based on current year
vegetative production (FFO, BLM, 1995).

tributary of the Colorado River Drainage System and current conditions
that do not meet the fundamentals of rangeland health.
